title: From This Side of the Door

blocks.text: Intro
80 BPM, 4/4; sparse nylon-string guitar figure, gently wavering harmonium; kettle hiss stretched into a faint, airy drone
Verse 1
deep, close baritone; warm grain, conversational phrasing, dry humor; leave space between the lines

Your bag caught on the railing.
You laughed and pulled it free.
I held the door a little wider,
Said, “Don’t you worry about me.”
Your headlights slid across the kitchen,
Then the corner ate the car.
I stood there with my shoes on
Till the room went dark.
Chorus
round bass enters; melody rises gently on “fine”; harmonium breathes between phrases

I told you I’d be fine
And I meant it when I swore.
But I still know your footsteps
From this side of the door.
Verse 2
soft kick, brushed snare and fingertips on wood establish a slow, loping groove; half-speak the last line with a small smile

There’s a notebook by the toaster
With coffee soaking through the page.
I’ve been working on the same four lines
For something like an age.
I can sing them to the kettle.
I can croon them to the dog.
When you ask me what I’m making,
I say, “Nothing,” laugh it off.
Chorus
bass clarinet enters with short, searching replies; vocal opens a little; keep the rhythm patient

I told you I’d be fine
And I meant it when I swore.
But I still know your footsteps
From this side of the door.
Verse 3
bowed cello gradually emerges beneath the groove; bass clarinet answers in the spaces; a faint metallic bell sounds in the distance

You called me from a station.
I could barely hear your voice.
I was halfway through a story
When you cut across the noise.
You said, “It’s been a long day.”
I had something good to say—
Some advice I thought would help you.
Then I shut up for a change.
Bridge
percussion and guitar fall away; expose the close voice over a low harmonium hum; let breath and hesitation remain audible

I nearly put the notebook back.
You asked about that sound.
I said, “I’m moving something,”
And I turned the kettle down.
There were dishes in the sink still.
There were words I meant to fix.
A quiet bass pulse returns; harmonium opens gently; take a breath before the invitation

I said, “I’ve got a thing here.
Got a minute? Listen to this.”
Final Chorus
the groove returns with deeper bass; cello rises, harmonium widens; baritone opens into a fuller melody

I told you I’d be fine
And I meant it when I swore.
Two higher, imperfect voices enter, answering the lead on the hook

But I still know your footsteps
From this side of the door.
Backing voices recede; lead stays close and tender as the instruments sustain around it

You could hear me turn the paper.
I could hear a train pull in.
I lost my place a little
Small breath; a smile in the voice
When you asked to hear it again.
Outro
rhythm, cello and clarinet fall away; close voice, single plucked guitar notes and the harmonium breathing out

The dog got up to check the hall,
Then settled on the floor.
I sang a little louder
From this side of the door.
One last plucked string resonates; harmonium fades into the sound of the room

notebook.style: Dark chamber folk with a slow soul groove, 80 BPM, 4/4. Deep, intimate baritone with warm grain, conversational phrasing, dry humor and restrained intensity. The voice sits close and clear, opening into melody on the chorus. Start with a sparse, repeating nylon-string guitar figure and the breath of a gently wavering harmonium. Add round bass and a loping rhythm made from a soft kick, brushed snare and fingertips on wood. Bass clarinet answers the singer in short, searching phrases. Let a bowed cello gradually emerge beneath the verses. Turn household textures into faint musical atmosphere: kettle hiss stretched into air, a small metallic tap softened into a distant bell. At the bridge, expose the voice over a low sustained hum. Build the final chorus through widening harmonies, deeper bass and two high, imperfect voices answering the hook. Keep the feeling tender, earthy, wry and quietly unsettled. End with close voice, one plucked string and the harmonium breathing out into the room.
